episode_title: The Truth About Allocation Mixes: What Advisors Get Wrong

real_qa.q: What are the three allocation mix categories that Track Advisor uses to classify financial advisory firms?
real_qa.r: Track Advisor breaks down allocation mixes into three categories: FIA heavy, meaning anything above 51% of annuity business; mid-range, which is anything between 51% and 75% of AUM; and AUM heavy, which is anything above 75% managed money.
real_qa.requete: Track Advisor allocation mix categories FIA AUM

real_qa.q: Why do AUM-heavy financial advisory firms have higher referral rates and better prospect conversion metrics than other allocation types?
real_qa.r: AUM-heavy offices had 30% of business from referrals versus 20% for other groups, and this higher referral volume improved their prospect story metrics substantially, including both stick rates and close rates, because referrals generally convert better than other lead sources.
real_qa.requete: AUM heavy firms referrals conversion rates

real_qa.q: What is the benchmark for cost per set and cost per client in financial advisory practices according to Track Advisor data?
real_qa.r: Cost per set benchmark should be about $1,000, while cost per client benchmark is $6,000. Cost per set reflects lead generation efficiency, while cost per client reflects how effectively a firm moves prospects through the sales process.
real_qa.requete: Track Advisor cost per set cost per client benchmark

real_qa.q: Why do FIA-heavy advisory firms have the highest cost per client despite maintaining benchmark cost per set?
real_qa.r: FIA-heavy firms stay within benchmark on cost per set ($1,000-$1,500) but have elevated cost per client ($8,000-$12,000) because they have the lowest stick rate and lowest kept second appointment rate, meaning they lose prospects before or at the first meeting, which increases the cost per client acquisition.
real_qa.requete: FIA heavy firms cost per client benchmark

real_qa.q: What major trend is emerging in conversion rates at live events according to Track Advisor's recent practice reviews?
real_qa.r: Approximately 60% of Track Advisor's top three business-moving recommendations in recent reviews focus on conversion rate issues, with advisors struggling to convert live event attendees to appointments and clients, even though live events remain profitable.
real_qa.requete: live events conversion rates financial advisors struggling

real_qa.q: What happens to financial advisory firm metrics when referral business masks underlying marketing funnel problems?
real_qa.r: When referrals make up a large portion of business, they can hide weak performance in other marketing funnels like dinner seminars; advisors may see strong overall close rates and stick rates from referrals while their other lead sources are actually failing, requiring separate analysis by funnel to identify problems.
real_qa.requete: referrals hide marketing funnel problems advisors

guest.bio_context: Erica Pauly has nearly 20 years of experience in the financial advisory industry, starting her career working with insurance-only advisors focused on annuities before eventually transitioning to holistic planning. She has tracked advisor progression and allocation shifts across multiple office types and now conducts comprehensive data analysis and behavioral reviews for financial advisory firms through Track Advisor.
